Carte Blanche's Christmas Special 2019

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Join Carte Blanche as we celebrate a truly South African Christmas

Unique Selling Point:
This will shot at the spectacular Glenshiel Manor in Westcliff with two wonderful South African talents; Nomulelo Yende and Teboho Moloi. The piece will be a celebration of Christmas, as well as acknowledging the wonderful work the Carte Blanche Making a difference has done thus far.

This will be a touching tribute to all South African considering the tough year we have had as a country.


Extra Budget Items:
Two cameramen.

Accommodation for Nombulelo Yende.

Return flights from Cape Town to OR Tambo international

Script:


Built in the 1930s,
King Edward VIII Hospital in KwaZulu-Natal
only had dark and derelict rooms
for treating critically ill children.
Large capital donations
to the Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust
made it possible to build a brand new facility –
from scratch.
The new Paediatric Centre of Excellence
opened in June 2012.
Rooms are now bright, light and modern.
It offers world-class,
dedicated paediatric facilities.
Over the past seven years
the Paediatric Centre has provided
consultation, high care and ICU services
over 200 000 times
to children in need.
The Nelson Mandela Medical School
at the University of KZN,
using King Edward VIII hospital,
produces 200 new doctors every year.
It’s among the largest output
of paediatricians in the country.
The Paediatric Centre’s facilities
provide a vital training ground
for many students.
The Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust
would like to thank
every donor, professional partner,
doctor, nurse,
porter and cleaner
for their contribution to this success.


GENERIC PROMO LINES 2019
The Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust
was created in 2008
to serve the children of South Africa.
The Trust assists vulnerable children
who are critically ill
and depend on public hospitals.
With the help of donors and specialist partners,
the Trust has completed 19 hospital projects
in 10 hospitals, in 6 provinces.
In 2019, the Trust handed over
a custom-designed 20-bed paediatric burns unit
at KwaZulu-Natal’s Ngwelezana hospital.
The Trust has another two projects
underway in other provinces.
The operating theatres, burns units,
ICUs and high care wards
that the Trust put in place
have provided the facilities
for hundreds of thousands of children
to receive the specialised help they need.
The majority of these facilities are used
in the training of doctors
and paediatricians nationwide.
We thank all the champions
who have helped us achieve these milestones.

Large capital donations to the Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust made it possible to build a brand new facility – from scratch. The new Paediatric Centre of Excellence opened in June 2012. Rooms are now bright, light and modern. It offers world-class, dedicated paediatric facilities. Over the past seven years the Paediatric Centre has provided consultation, high care and ICU services over 200 000 times to children in need. The Nelson Mandela Medical School at the University of KZN, using King Edward VIII hospital, produces 200 new doctors every year. It’s among the largest output of paediatricians in the country. The Paediatric Centre’s facilities provide a vital training ground for many students. The Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust would like to thank every donor, professional partner, doctor, nurse, porter and cleaner for their contribution to this success. GENERIC PROMO LINES 2019 The Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust was created in 2008 to serve the children of South Africa. The Trust assists vulnerable children who are critically ill and depend on public hospitals. With the help of donors and specialist partners, the Trust has completed 19 hospital projects in 10 hospitals, in 6 provinces. In 2019, the Trust handed over a custom-designed 20-bed paediatric burns unit at KwaZulu-Natal’s Ngwelezana hospital. The Trust has another two projects underway in other provinces. The operating theatres, burns units, ICUs and high care wards that the Trust put in place have provided the facilities for hundreds of thousands of children to receive the specialised help they need. The majority of these facilities are used in the training of doctors and paediatricians nationwide. We thank all the champions who have helped us achieve these milestones.
